content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To hang planters with knotted rope, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Attach the ceiling hooks (20 minutes)
Step 2. Purchase a spool of heavy-duty cotton rope (45 minutes)
Step 3. Measure and cut four equal lengths of rope (10 minutes)
Step 4. Research various decorative knot patterns (1 hour)
Step 5. Sketch the design for the rope hanger (15 minutes)
Step 6. Select the ceramic pots for the plants (30 minutes)
Step 7. Hang the finished assembly on the ceiling hook (5 minutes)
Step 8. Gather a measuring tape and fabric scissors (5 minutes)
Step 9. Tighten the final structural knots (5 minutes)
Step 10. Mark the rope at 12-inch intervals for knot placement (15 minutes)
Step 11. Create a loop at the top of the rope bundle (10 minutes)
Step 12. Practice tying a basic square knot (20 minutes)
Step 13. Trim the excess rope from the bottom fringe (5 minutes)
Step 14. Sort the ropes into pairs for the first row (5 minutes)
Step 15. Place the planter into the rope cradle (2 minutes)
Step 16. Tie the first set of square knots (25 minutes)
Step 17. Inspect the rope for any frays or weak spots (5 minutes)
Step 18. Adjust the tension of the side ropes (10 minutes)
Step 19. Bind the top of the ropes with a gathering knot (15 minutes)
Step 20. Clear a large workspace on the floor (10 minutes)
Step 21. Secure the top loop to a temporary working hook (5 minutes)
Step 22. Watch a tutorial on macrame techniques (30 minutes)
Step 23. Wash and dry the ceramic pots (20 minutes)
Step 24. Thread the ropes through a decorative wooden ring (10 minutes)
Step 25. Untangle the cut rope segments (10 minutes)
Step 26. Clean the workspace of any debris (15 minutes)
Step 27. Tie a large base knot to support the pot weight (10 minutes)
Step 28. Buy bags of potting soil (30 minutes)
Step 29. Mix the soil with perlite for drainage (15 minutes)
Step 30. Tie the second row of alternating square knots (25 minutes)
Step 31. Choose a location with good sunlight (10 minutes)
Step 32. Drill pilot holes in the ceiling joists (15 minutes)
Step 33. Label each rope end with masking tape (10 minutes)
Step 34. Check the rope length requirements for the pot size (5 minutes)
Step 35. Purchase healthy indoor plants (1 hour)
Step 36. Water the plants thoroughly (10 minutes)
Step 37. Practice tying a spiral hitch knot (20 minutes)
Step 38. Lightly singe the rope ends to prevent unraveling (10 minutes)
Step 39. Level the pot within the rope structure (10 minutes)
Step 40. Repot the plants into the ceramic pots (30 minutes)
Step 41. Add decorative beads to the rope strands (40 minutes)
Step 42. Fill the bottom of the pots with drainage rocks (10 minutes)
Step 43. Comb out the rope fringe at the bottom (15 minutes)
Step 44. Add a layer of moss to the top of the soil (10 minutes)
Step 45. Wipe down the exterior of the pots (5 minutes)
Step 46. Insert a slow-release fertilizer spike (2 minutes)
Step 47. Take a photo of the completed pots (5 minutes)
Step 48. Transfer the potted plants to the staging area (10 minutes)
Step 49. Lay out the ropes parallel to each other (5 minutes)
Step 50. Double-check the symmetry of the knots (15 minutes)
Step 51. Look for a step ladder in the garage (15 minutes)
Step 52. Position the ladder under the ceiling hook (5 minutes)
Step 53. Tie the final row of knots to form the basket (20 minutes)
Step 54. Verify the pot sits level in the ropes (5 minutes)
Step 55. Test the strength of the knots with a heavy weight (5 minutes)
Step 56. Seal the rope ends with a dab of glue (15 minutes)
Step 57. Adjust the height of the planter (10 minutes)
Step 58. Organize the remaining craft supplies (20 minutes)
Step 59. Clean up the dust from the floor (10 minutes)
Step 60. Check that the planter is securely fastened (2 minutes)
